{{Quote|Once we were mighty Jedi of the Republic, brothers in the Force. But the Great Schism between the dark side and the light turned Jedi against Jedi. Our ancestors were defeated, driven off&hellip; cast out!|[[Marka Ragnos]]|<ref name="Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]]</ref>}}
The '''Hundred-Year Darkness''', also known as the '''Hundred-Year War''', was a conflict that began in [[7000 BBY]] and lasted until approximately [[6900 BBY]], when a group of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] created monstrous armies to battle the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The Hundred-Year Darkness began three years after the Dark Jedi split with the Order in the [[Second Great Schism]]. After a century of fighting, the Dark Jedi lost the war at the [[Battle of Corbos]], but went on to conquer [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] and found the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].

==Beginnings==
{{Quote|So envious were the Jedi Knights of our ability to transform creatures into improved manifestations, they made it their ongoing duty to hunt us&mdash;the Dark Jedi&mdash;wherever we attempted to experiment and practice our knowledge.|Ajunta Pall|<ref name="JvS" />}}
The [[Second Great Schism]] began when a group of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] began practicing extended uses of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Dark side of the Force]]. By relying more and more upon the dark side, these Jedi learned that using the Force of sufficient intensity could bend life itself.<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> With their new powers, the Knights experimented upon other lifeforms to create monsters as extensions of their will. Other Jedi looked upon these new powers with horror. The earliest rebels, the [[Legions of Lettow]], had been defeated in the [[First Great Schism]], but their legacy remained, and a second group of dissidents would emerge,<ref name="TOR">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 22: The Second Great Schism}}</ref> led by [[Ajunta Pall]].<ref name="Tomb of Ajunta Pall">{{TORcite|type=codex|Tomb of Ajunta Pall}}</ref>

All [[Great Schism/Legends|great conflicts]] began with passion, and this one was no different. Firmly adamant in protecting their newly-acquired powers, this sect of Jedi sought to convince the other Jedi to embrace the Dark Side instead of fearing it. The others were not convinced. Firmly convinced that their way was right, the arguments turned into conflict.<ref name="BoS" /> The [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] were exiled along with their teachings. A war had begun that would last a hundred years.<ref name="TOR" />

==War==
{{Quote|A Jedi sect, weren't they? The result of a kind of family feud.|A young [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], recalling his knowledge of the Sith's creation|<ref name="Darth Plagueis (novel)">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Corbosbattle.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Jedi and Dark Jedi fight at the [[Battle of Corbos]]]]

During the war, the Jedi constructed the [[The Prism|Prism]], a secret prison facility known only to the members of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]].<ref name="Darth Vader and the Ghost Prison 3">[[Darth Vader and the Ghost Prison 3|''Darth Vader and the Ghost Prison'' 3]]</ref>

As the war went on, [[Sorzus Syn]] created [[Shambler]]s, [[Howler]]s, [[Pit Horror]]s, and ultimately, [[Leviathan (creature)|Leviathans]], creatures that could suck life essences into blister-traps on their backs.<ref name="BoS" />

The [[Battle of Corbos|last stand]] of the Dark Jedi was on the world of [[Corbos]]. With the help of infighting,<ref name="TOR" /> the Dark Jedi were defeated.<ref name="JvS" />

===Exile===
{{Quote|Thousands of years ago, the Jedi had another civil war that split the Order. It was a... terrible thing. A faction among the Jedi abandoned the teachings of the order, following their own path. They waged war on their fellow Jedi, a war that raged across the galaxy. But these fallen Jedi were cast out, defeated, and they retreated to worlds in the Outer Rim. Over time, they took on the mantle of the Lords of the Sith. But in their hearts, they never forgot the Jedi. The hatred for the Jedi Order burns in their veins like fire, and echoes in their teachings.|[[Kreia]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Exodus1.jpg|thumb|300px|The [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] are exiled.]]
After their defeat on Corbos, the surviving Dark Jedi were rounded up by the Jedi. The [[Exiles]], as they became known to the Jedi, were stripped of their weapons and navigational instruments, herded onto unarmed<ref name="JvS" /> [[Dark Jedi galleon|galleons]], and banished beyond known space.<ref name="Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2" /><ref name="BoS" />

The Hundred-Year Darkness was over, and the Jedi had weathered the Second Great Schism.<ref name="BoS" />

==A new world==
{{Quote|The surviving Dark Siders fled the Republic, finally coming to Korriban where the native Sith welcomed them as gods.|[[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|Darth Wyyrlok III]]|<ref name="Legacy30" />}}
[[File:Jedi_exile_JMGD.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The primitive [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] witness the arrival of the [[exiles]].]]
Inspired by rumors of the [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|Kingdom of Sith]], Sorzus Syn guided the Dark Jedi to [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. [[Discovery of Korriban|Landing]] on the world, they found that true to the rumors, it was inhabited by a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] species calling themselves the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]]. [[Hakagram Graush]], the [[Sith King|King of the Sith]], was shocked at the appearance of the outsiders, but after witnessing their powers and advanced technology, the king welcomed the exiled Jedi to the world. However, this led to Graush's downfall. Graush's [[Shadow Hand]] conspired with the new arrivals, and betrayed his liege to the Dark Jedi. Using his training in the Force, Ajunta Pall beheaded Graush, convincing the Sith that the Exiles were gods. The Exiles became the rulers of the Sith and came to be called the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lords of the Sith]]. [[Ajunta Pall]] became the first [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] and established the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="BoS" />

[[File:XoxaanMuur.jpg|thumb|300px|[[XoXaan]] and [[Karness Muur]] are greeted by the Sith.]]

Sorzus Syn learned the prophecy of the ''[[Sith'ari/Legends|Sith'ari]]'' from the Sith. The ''Sith'ari'' was a perfect being who would one day lead the Sith. According to prophecy, the ''Sith'ari'' would rise up and destroy the Sith, but in the process make them stronger than ever before. Syn saw this as a striking parallel to the [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]] of Jedi legend and speculated that she was the ''Sith'ari''.<ref name="BoS" />

==Return==
After becoming Sith Lords, several Exiles took the ship they had arrived on along with new weapons, [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors, and their new secrets of [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]] in an [[First battle between Jedi and Sith|attempt to destroy the Jedi]] against Ajunta Pall's orders, only to have themselves destroyed, and giving the Jedi the knowledge that [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Space]] existed, and that the Exiles had survived.<ref name="JvS" />

==Legacy==
As time passed, and interbreeding occurred between the Exiles and the Sith, the term "Sith" came to mean not only the species, but also their fallen Jedi masters. When they first met the Exiles, the Sith wore primitive clothing. With the influence of the Exiles, elaborate clothing came into use.<ref name="Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2" />

In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Odan-Urr/Legends|Odan-Urr]] believed that the Hundred-Year Darkness started with the First Great Schism,<ref name="GAS0" /> as did the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Historical Council]] in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]],<ref name="TEC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> but by [[36 ABY]], the Historical Council had learned that the Hundred-Year Darkness began with the Second Great Schism.<ref name="NEC" />

Later in 5000 BBY,<ref name="NEC" /> the Sith Empire [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|invaded the Republic]] under the leadership of [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]],<ref name="Fall 3">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 3]]</ref> a descendent of the Exiles who wanted revenge for the banishment of his ancestors.<ref name="Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|While the details are lost in the mists of time, Galactic historians believe there has been a rift between the light side and the dark side of the Force almost since the foundation of the Jedi Order some 25,000 standard years before the Battle of Yavin. Many think it was one rogue Jedi who fell to the dark side, turned others, and eventually built an entire army of dark siders. For the next century, a deadly war swept the galaxy, destroying planets and civilizations before the Jedi Knights prevailed.|[[Stephen J. Sansweet]]|<ref name="Ask">{{SWArchive|url=community/askjc/steve/askjc20000619.html|text=Ask the Lucasfilm Jedi Council - June 19, 2000}}</ref>}}
The first reference to fallen Jedi becoming the rulers of the "Sith civilization" to be published was in [[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 1]].<ref name="TFU">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 1]]</ref> This information was again mentioned in [[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 1|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 1]].<ref name="DLOTS1">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 1|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 1]]</ref> The first mention of the name "the Hundred-Year Darkness" was in [[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 3]] in a list of events involving the Dark Side. No further information about it was mentioned.<ref name="DLOTS3">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 3]]</ref>

In the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] book [[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 0|''Tales of the Jedi - The Golden Age of the Sith'' 0]], published on [[July 31]], [[1996]]<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54589/star_wars_tales_of_the_jedi_-_the_golden_age_of_the_sith_1996|text=Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi - The Golden Age of the Sith (1996)}}</ref> by [[Dark Horse Comics]],<ref name="DarkHorse">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/95-416/Star-Wars-Tales-of-the-Jedi---The-Golden-Age-of-the-Sith-0-of-5|text=Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi - The Golden Age of the Sith #0 (of 5)}}</ref> a young Jedi, Odan-Urr, conveys tales of the Sith to [[Ooroo/Legends|Master Ooroo]], recounting that "Dark Jedi" of "the First Great Schism of the Jedi Knights"  were "defeated after a century of bloodshed" and that the "Jedi Exiles", noted as such in the text of issue 0, subsequently "forged the Sith civilization into a new empire".<ref name="GAS0" /> In [[1996]]'s [[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi'' – ''The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]], the [[Force ghost/Legends|ghost]] of [[Marka Ragnos]] recounts how this "Great Schism between the Dark Side and the Light turned Jedi against Jedi." Ragnos goes on to say that it has been "many centuries" since then. In the same issue, Odan-Urr tells [[Teta/Legends|Teta]] that "it has been many centuries" since "evil Jedi" were "banished".<ref name="TOTJ 2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> In [[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi'' – ''The Golden Age of the Sith'' 4]], Odan-Urr warns the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] about "exiled Jedi, defeated millennia ago".<ref name="TOTJ 4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 4]]</ref>

''[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|The Essential Chronology]]'' ([[2000]]), described "a century of bloodshed" associated with "the first great schism within the Jedi Knights" "millennia" and "centuries" before the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]].<ref name="TEC" />

Elaborating on comments made by [[Stephen J. Sansweet]] via the [[StarWars.com]]'s ''[[Ask the Lucasfilm Jedi Council]]'' feature in [[2000]],<ref name="Ask" /> ''[[Star Wars: Secrets of the Sith]]'' ([[2000]]), by [[Iain R. Morris]], [[Benjamin Harper|Ben Harper]] and [[Marc Cerasini]], placed the "first uprising of the dark side" and subsequent "century-long battle" somewhere between "25,000-5,000 B.B.Y.", and further described the idea that galactic historians believed that one rogue Jedi Knight was responsible for turning fellow Knights, which then led to the creation of a "fleet of spacecraft" used against the Jedi during the "next hundred years."<ref name="SWSotS">''[[Star Wars: Secrets of the Sith]]''</ref>

[[Arden Lyn]]'s biography in [[Abel G. Peña]]'s "[[The Emperor's Pawns]]", a collection of biographies that were published in [[Star Wars Gamer 5|''Star Wars Gamer'' #5]] ([[2001]]), stated that "Xendor and his minions wreaked havoc during the First Great Schism" while the attached "Adventure Seed: Life After Death", stated that Arden was "twisted after 250 centuries of 'death,'" meaning the First Great Schism took place approximately 25,000 years prior to her reawakening.<ref name="tep">{{GamerCite|5|The Emperor's Pawns}}</ref> On [[June 29]], [[2006]], Abel revealed that he had exorcised portions of his article, "[[Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties]]" related to a Second Great Schism in [[10,000 BBY]].<ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=posts/24255327|board=Literature|thread=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties|user=[[Abel G. Peña|Halagad_Ventor]]|PTtime=2006-06-29|quote=...I never updated the Sorcerers of Tund section of Evil Never Dies (which originally had them as a group of Jedi schismatics of an intellectually rather than violently motivated Second Great Schism, placed around 10,000 BBY)...|archiveurl=https://boards.theforce.net/threads/evil-never-dies-the-sith-dynasties.24202765/page-9#post-24255327}}</ref>

''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]'' ([[2001]]), released only a month after ''The Emperor's Pawns'', did not mention Xendor or Arden Lyn, only describing "the first dark side uprising" that took place "during this ancient period" and that this battle lasted "more than a century" prior to these "Dark Jedi" discovering the Sith.<ref name="TDSSB">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The timeline in the beginning of ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' ([[2002]]) listed "The First Great Schism between followers of the dark side and the light side occurs. After more than a century, the dark-siders are driven off into the wilds of the galaxy" under the heading "circa [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 B.B.Y.]]" while also having the "The Jedi Knights lead the Republic through the Hundred-Year Darkness" under the heading of "circa [[7000 BBY|7,000 B.B.Y.]]."<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>

[[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]]'s biography in ''The New Essential Guide to Characters'' says, "The First Great Schism between the light and dark sides of the Force occured in the early years of the Old Republic. Certain Jedi turned to the dark side, and when defeated, they fled the civilized galaxy and conquered a primitive species-the Sith. They made themselves the Lords of the Sith, and named the greatest among them the Dark Lord. Naga Sadow, heir to this wicked tradition, became the first Sith Lord in nearly twenty millennia to reestablish contact with the forgotten Republic".<ref name="NEGC" />

''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' ([[2005]]) reasserted that the Hundred-Year Darkness occured ~7000 BBY, but also revealed it to be the same event as the "century of bloodshed" mentioned in ''Tales of the Jedi - The Golden Age of the Sith'' 0 and to now follow a "Second Great Schism" while the "First Great Schism" was [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] to be a separate event.<ref name="NEC" /> In spite of this retcon, ''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Special Edition]]'', which was published in [[May]] [[2007]],<ref name="SDate">{{DK|host=dorlingkindersley-uk.co.uk|url=nf/Book/BookDisplay/0,,9781405318686,00.html|text=Star Wars the Ultimate Visual Guide|nolive=1}}</ref> and ''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Updated and Expanded]]'', which was published on [[April 30]], [[2012]],<ref name="UDate">{{DK|subdomain=us|url=nf/Book/BookDisplay/0,,9780756692483,00.html|text=Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Updated and Expanded|nolive=1}}</ref> say that the Exiles turned to the dark side "in the early years of the Old Republic."<ref name="UVGSE">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Special Edition]]''</ref><ref name="UVGUE">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Updated and Expanded]]''</ref>

When asked about this retcon, [[Daniel Wallace]], author of ''The New Esssential Chronology'', said it was because of "LFL internal documents" dating Dark Jedi contact with the Sith species at ~7000 BBY.<ref name="NECt">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2005/10/new-essential-chronology-talkback.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=The New Essential Chronology: Talkback thread}}</ref> On [[January 11]], 2006, [[Leland Chee]] said that this retcon was to "correct the the [sic] original discrepency of the timing of the Great Schism introduced by ''The New Essential Guide to Characters''."<ref name="Leland Chee">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=630|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2006-01-11|time=04:12 PM}}</ref> On [[June 30]], 2006, Abel G. Peña stated that he "didn't quite understand this realignment of the origins of the Sith."<ref name="JCFAbel">{{JCFCite|url=posts/24263085|board=Literature|thread=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties|user=[[Abel G. Peña|Halagad_Ventor]]|PTtime=2006-06-29|quote=I didn't quite understand this realignment of the origins of the Sith either, but at least for now it is what it is.|archiveurl=https://boards.theforce.net/threads/evil-never-dies-the-sith-dynasties.24202765/page-10#post-24263085}}</ref>
